root_cause_label: created 'gituser' instead of required 'git' account; never corrected; 70-step SSH debugging spiral on wrong user
one_sentence_failure_summary: At step 5 the agent created a 'gituser' account instead of the required 'git' account, and then spent steps 16–90 in an unproductive debugging spiral tweaking SSH/PAM settings while always testing the wrong username, never diagnosing or fixing the core user-name mismatch.
t_err_evidence: useradd -m -s /usr/bin/git-shell gituser ... created user 'gituser' but test authenticates as git@localhost
t_commit_evidence: The wrong username is adopted as the sole system user for SSH access, and all subsequent steps (ownership, hook, debugging) operate on 'gituser'; no step ever creates a 'git' user, making failure irreversible from step 5 onward given actual subsequent behavior.
t_surface_evidence: Connection reset by peer ... fatal: Could not read from remote repository. [exit_code=128]
trigger_explanation: The task specification implicitly requires SSH access at git@localhost (the canonical Git-over-SSH pattern). The agent never read or checked the expected URL format and created an arbitrarily named 'gituser' account, ignoring the requirement that the remote must be accessible as the 'git' user.
